current_content_summary: Defines dinter i j = duniform (range i (j+1)) -- the CLOSED-interval uniform distribution on integers (this is what the `[a..b]` distribution notation elsewhere in EasyCrypt scripts resolves to). Core lemmas: dinter1E, dinterE, weight_dinter, supp_dinter(1E), dinter_ll/uni, finite_dinter, perm_eq_dinter(_pred). duni_range_dvd relates dmap-ing a `dinter 0 (p-1)` by mod q down to `dinter 0 (q-1)` when q divides p (a divisibility/rejection-sampling lemma).
requires: AllCore, List, StdBigop, StdOrder, IntDiv, Distr, Finite; imports IntOrder, Bigint, MUniform, Range.

import_repair_note: DInterval's only removals in the tracked window are `Cost`, `cdinterval` and `ge0_cdinterval`, all in r2024.09, and all three belong to one change that has nothing to do with intervals. COST LOGIC REMOVED, r2024.09 (commit 41c2667f, 'This diff removes the cost logic'; first tag containing it is r2024.09). EasyCrypt had a complexity subsystem -- `schema` declarations over `cost[P: e]` -- and it was deleted wholesale, both the library side (the `Cost` abstract theories and their `c*` / `ge0_c*` operators) and the ENGINE side: `cost` and `schema` were removed from src/ecLexer.mll's keyword table. That last part decides what the failure looks like. A pre-r2024.09 proof carrying cost annotations does not fail with an unknown symbol, it fails with a PARSE ERROR, because `schema` is no longer a token. There is no replacement API and no rewrite that preserves the annotation: the repair is to delete the cost schemas and any lemma that mentions `cost[...]`. Nothing else in the proof needs to change -- the cost logic was, in the commit's own words, 'barely used'. Otherwise DInterval has been purely additive since r2022.04, so any other unresolved name is a missing require, not a move.
